Lands in the valleys of Sarpy, and East Sarpy Creeks adjacent to the leases are irrigable, but are not presently under irrigation.

Because mining will not extend into these valleys, effects on irrigable lands will be negligible.
Inmigration due to increased employment provided by mining is expected to be concentrated in Hardin. Expansion of Hardin will necessarily encroach on irrigated cropland in the Big Horn River valley. On the average, it is expected that construction of each new single family dwelling will result in the loss of about 1/4 acre of irrigated cropland.
Grazing Land
Grazing on native or reseeded grasslands and woodlands comprises the largest current usage of Tracts II and III; over 90 percent of the area is used for grazing. Assuming that all of the 2,275 acres of cropland are within the 25,000 acres to be mined, the remainder, or 22,725 acres, consists of grazing land. This corresponds to approximately 7,575 AUM's (animal unit months) per year, or sufficient acreage for the grazing of about 750 cow-calf units assuming a 10 month grazing season.
